html:
Le Joola was a ferry owned by the government of Senegal that capsized off the coast of the Gambia on the night of 26 September 2002. At least 1,863 people died and only 64 survived, which makes it one of the worst shipwrecks in peacetime.

The ship ran between Ziguinchor in the Casamance region and Dakar, the capital. For people in Casamance it was a lifeline: the road north crosses the Gambia, and a long rebellion in the region made travel by land slow and risky.

The ferry was built for well under 600 passengers but carried around 2,000 that night, many without tickets, among them students heading back to school. A storm struck, and the overloaded ship rolled over within minutes. Most passengers were Senegalese; others came from Gambia, France and elsewhere.

The disaster caused fury in Senegal. President Abdoulaye Wade dismissed his government weeks later. More people died than on the Titanic, yet the sinking is little known outside West Africa and France.
sum: Le Joola was a ferry owned by the government of Senegal that capsized off the coast of the Gambia on the night of 26 September 2002. At least 1,863 people died and only 64 survived, which makes it one of the worst shipwrecks in peacetime.
